ei.title: Navigating the World of Artificial Satellites
ei.subject: 영어1

fullPassage:
Navigating the World of Artificial Satellites

For years, people have gazed at the sky, wondering about the mysteries of the world beyond. This curiosity has led to the exploration of the universe, and as a result, space is no longer an unknown territory. Since the launch of the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, in 1957, the world has witnessed the blossoming of space exploration.

Satellites and Satellite Data

As you look up at the night sky, you may have seen a bright, twinkling star and wondered if it was a star or a satellite. Satellites play a vital role in space science, and their development has opened up a new era of space travel and research.

Satellites are machines launched into space that orbit the Earth. They gather data from every corner of the globe, from wheat fields in Zambia to glaciers in Antarctica. Once collected, the satellite data are transmitted back to the ground station to be analyzed and turned into useful information that people can use in their everyday lives. During this process, the data are reviewed by the scientists before they are sent out to users.

Uses of Satellites

Satellites are used in various fields, such as communication, navigation, weather forecasting, scientific research, and Earth observation. Firstly, satellite data play a crucial role in facilitating global communication by supporting TV signals, radio broadcasts, internet connections, and telephone calls. Additionally, navigation satellites transmit signals used by the Global Positioning System (GPS) to determine the location of objects on Earth. If you have a GPS receiver, these satellites can help you precisely locate your destination. Moreover, satellites collect data on weather patterns to provide forecasts. Satellites are also extensively used for scientific research and experiments that explore the Earth's atmosphere, other planets, and stars.

Satellite data are invaluable for observation and monitoring purposes as well. For example, high-resolution satellite images provide information that is useful for various purposes, including military surveillance.

And that is not all. In the field of agriculture, satellites are useful for enhancing crop management and production. They monitor crop health and predict crop yields during the harvest season. It is also known that satellite data can help to estimate market sales based on the number of cars in parking lots. This information helps develop effective marketing strategies and make informed decisions for higher profits.

Most importantly, satellite images are used to locate emergency situations. For example, in the event of a disaster, satellite images can help locate blocked roads or damaged buildings, allowing rescuers to find people in time. Satellites can monitor almost any part of the globe, identifying, predicting, and managing what is happening around the world.

Challenges in Satellite Technology

The increasing number of satellites launched into orbit has caused problems, one of which is space debris. Nearly half of the satellites in orbit are no longer in use. However, they continue to orbit the Earth at high speeds and sometimes collide with other satellites. These impacts have created up to 1 million pieces of space debris, which can damage satellites already in orbit and pose a threat to future space missions.

Another problem is the light pollution from satellites. Enormous numbers of low-flying satellites have been launched into space, and this is expected to continue. Although they don't generate their own light, these satellites and pieces of space debris reflect sunlight, contributing to the brightness of the night sky. It is predicted that by 2030, the night sky will be up to 12 percent brighter than its natural darkness. This means that in the near future we may not be able to see the stars anymore.

In addition, the development of satellite technology is closely tied to unequal access to information. Some countries lack satellites or the capability to analyze satellite data, while others have launched hundreds of them and created a vast pool of information. Approximately 37 percent of the global population remains unconnected to the internet, unable to fully benefit from satellite-based services. This difference in access results in an uneven distribution of satellite information collected from space.

In conclusion, while satellite technology has revolutionized the world, it still has limitations and challenges. Addressing these issues is crucial for building a promising future for space exploration. The space industry also needs to share responsibility and collaborate to properly use satellite technology. Only then can we ensure an equal distribution of resources and information, benefiting all humans on Earth.

Satellites Launched by Korea

Several satellites have been launched in Korea, each with a specific purpose. The first one was Korea Institute of Technology Satellite-1 (KITSAT-1), which was launched in 1992 for scientific research and experimentation. It is also known as "Our Star 1." The next one was KOREASAT-1 in 1995, which was Korea's first communication satellite. Since 1999, Korea has launched KOMPSAT-1, for various purposes, and COMS, for monitoring weather and the oceans. Then, in 2020, Anasis 2 was launched for military surveillance. In 2023, NEXTSAT-2 and seven other satellites were launched using a domestically developed rocket, Nuri.

questions.passage: Satellites play a (A)[vital / trivial] role in space science, and their development has opened up a new era of space travel and research. Satellites are machines launched into space that orbit the Earth. They gather data from every corner of the globe, from wheat fields in Zambia to glaciers in Antarctica. Once collected, the satellite data are (B)[transmitted / concealed] back to the ground station to be (C)[analyzed / ignored] and turned into useful information that people can use in their everyday lives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 위성은 우주과학에서 중요한(vital) 역할을 한다. 수집된 데이터는 지상국으로 전송되어(transmitted) 분석된다(analyzed).
det.analysis:
✅ ② vital–transmitted–analyzed: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ① trivial(사소한)은 vital의 반의어
❌ ③ concealed(숨겨진)과 ignored(무시된)가 원문과 반대
❌ ④ trivial이 부적합
det.tip: vital(중요한) ↔ trivial(사소한) / transmitted(전송된) ↔ concealed(숨겨진) / analyzed(분석된) ↔ ignored(무시된)

questions.passage: Uses of Satellites Satellites are used in various fields, such as communication, navigation, weather forecasting, scientific research, and Earth observation. Firstly, satellite data play a (A)[crucial / insignificant] role in facilitating global communication by supporting TV signals, radio broadcasts, internet connections, and telephone calls. Additionally, navigation satellites transmit signals used by the Global Positioning System (GPS) to determine the location of objects on Earth. If you have a GPS receiver, these satellites can help you (B)[precisely / vaguely] locate your destination. Moreover, satellites collect data on weather patterns to provide forecasts. Satellites are also (C)[extensively / rarely] used for scientific research and experiments that explore the Earth's atmosphere, other planets, and stars.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 위성 데이터는 글로벌 통신을 촉진하는 데 결정적인(crucial) 역할을 한다. GPS로 목적지를 정확하게(precisely) 찾을 수 있다. 과학 연구에도 광범위하게(extensively) 사용된다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ crucial–precisely–extensively: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ① insignificant(중요하지 않은)는 crucial의 반의어
❌ ② vaguely(모호하게)는 precisely의 반의어
❌ ③ rarely(거의 ~않는)는 extensively의 반의어
det.tip: crucial(결정적인) ↔ insignificant(하찮은) / precisely(정확하게) ↔ vaguely(모호하게) / extensively(광범위하게) ↔ rarely(드물게)

questions.passage: However, they continue to orbit the Earth at high speeds and sometimes (A)[collide / align] with other satellites. These impacts have created up to 1 million pieces of space debris, which can damage satellites already in orbit and pose a threat to future space missions. Another problem is the light pollution from satellites. Enormous numbers of low-flying satellites have been launched into space, and this is expected to continue. Although they don't generate their own light, these satellites and pieces of space debris reflect sunlight, (B)[contributing / reducing] to the brightness of the night sky. It is predicted that by 2030, the night sky will be up to 12 percent brighter than its natural darkness. This means that in the near future we may not be able to see the stars anymore. In addition, the development of satellite technology is closely tied to unequal access to information. Some countries lack satellites or the capability to analyze satellite data, while others have launched hundreds of them and created a vast pool of information. Approximately 37 percent of the global population remains unconnected to the internet, unable to fully benefit from satellite-based services. This difference in access results in an (C)[uneven / balanced] distribution of satellite information collected from space.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 위성들이 빠른 속도로 다른 위성과 충돌한다(collide). 우주 잔해가 밤하늘 밝기에 기여한다(contributing). 위성 정보의 불균등한(uneven) 분배를 초래한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① collide–contributing–uneven: 모두 원문 그대로 적합
❌ ② align(정렬하다)은 collide의 반의어
❌ ③ reducing(줄이는)은 contributing의 반의어, balanced(균형 잡힌)는 uneven의 반의어
❌ ④ balanced가 uneven의 반의어
det.tip: collide(충돌하다) ↔ align(정렬하다) / contributing(기여하는) ↔ reducing(줄이는) / uneven(불균등한) ↔ balanced(균형 잡힌)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ③ decline(쇠퇴)이 부적절 → 원문은 blossoming(개화). 최초 위성 발사 이후 탐사가 꽃피웠다는 맥락.
❌ ① curiosity: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ② exploration: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ witnessed: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: blossoming(개화, 번성) ↔ decline(쇠퇴). 문맥 단서: 'first artificial satellite' 발사 이후 발전

questions.passage: In the field of agriculture, satellites are useful for ①<u>enhancing</u> crop management and production.  They monitor crop health and ②<u>neglect</u> crop yields during the harvest season.  It is also known that satellite data can help to estimate market sales based on the number of cars in parking lots.  This information helps develop ③<u>effective</u> marketing strategies and make ④<u>informed</u> decisions for higher profits.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 위성은 작물 건강을 모니터링하고 수확량을 ②무시한다→예측한다(predict). 농업 분야에서 위성의 유용성을 설명하는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ② neglect(무시하다)이 부적절 → 원문은 predict(예측하다). 수확기 작물 수확량을 예측한다는 맥락.
❌ ① enhancing: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ③ effective: 원문 그대로 적절
❌ ④ informed: 원문 그대로 적절
det.tip: predict(예측하다) ↔ neglect(무시하다). 문맥 단서: monitor crop health and ~ crop yields

det.korean: 전 세계 인구의 약 37%가 인터넷에 ④연결되어→연결되지 않은 채(unconnected) 남아있다. 위성 기반 서비스의 혜택을 온전히 누리지 못한다는 맥락.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ connected(연결된)가 부적절 → 원문은 unconnected(연결되지 않은). 정보 불균등 접근 문제를 설명하는 맥락.
❌ ① debris: 원문 그대로 적절 (우주 잔해)
❌ ② reflect: 원문 그대로 적절 (햇빛을 반사)
❌ ③ brightness: 원문 그대로 적절 (밤하늘 밝기)
det.tip: unconnected(연결되지 않은) ↔ connected(연결된). 문맥 단서: 'unable to fully benefit from satellite-based services'

questions.passage: Satellites are machines launched into space that __________ the Earth.  They gather data from every corner of the globe, from wheat fields in Zambia to glaciers in Antarctica.  Once collected, the satellite data are transmitted back to the ground station to be analyzed and turned into useful information that people can use in their everyday lives.  During this process, the data are reviewed by the scientists before they are sent out to users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 위성은 지구를 궤도를 돌다(orbit)하는 우주로 발사된 기계이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ orbit: 궤도를 돌다 — 'machines launched into space that ____ the Earth'에 적합
❌ ① launch: 발사하다 — 이미 launched가 있음, 의미 중복
❌ ② observe: 관찰하다 — 위성이 지구를 관찰한다고 하기엔 문맥 불충분
❌ ④ connect: 연결하다 — 지구를 연결한다는 의미 불분명
det.tip: orbit the Earth = 지구 궤도를 돌다. satellite의 기본 기능

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 위성 데이터는 관찰과 모니터링 목적에 매우 귀중하다(invaluable).
det.analysis:
✅ ① invaluable: 매우 귀중한 — 관찰·모니터링에 필수적이라는 맥락에 적합
❌ ② irrelevant: 무관한 — 문맥과 반대
❌ ③ unavoidable: 불가피한 — 가치가 아닌 필연성을 나타냄
❌ ④ invisible: 보이지 않는 — 데이터의 속성과 무관
det.tip: invaluable = priceless = extremely valuable (매우 귀중한). in-이 부정이 아닌 강조

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 이 문제들을 해결하는 것은 우주 탐사의 유망한(promising) 미래를 구축하는 데 중요하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ promising: 유망한 — 미래를 긍정적으로 묘사하며, 문제 해결의 목적과 부합
❌ ① threatening: 위협적인 — 문제 해결 결과로 위협적 미래는 부적합
❌ ② declining: 쇠퇴하는 — 긍정적 결론과 모순
❌ ③ uncertain: 불확실한 — 문제 해결 후에도 불확실하다면 결론 논리 붕괴
det.tip: promising future = 유망한 미래. Addressing these issues is crucial for building a ~ future

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>gazed</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 수년간 하늘을 응시해 왔다(gazed).
det.analysis:
✅ ② stared: 응시하다 — gazed와 동의어 (오래 바라보다)
❌ ① glanced: 흘끗 보다 — 짧게 보는 것
❌ ③ blinked: 눈을 깜빡이다 — 바라보는 것과 다름
❌ ④ squinted: 눈을 가늘게 뜨다 — 바라보는 방식이 다름
det.tip: gaze = stare = look steadily (응시하다). glance는 '흘끗 보다'로 반대 뉘앙스

Satellites are used in various fields, such as communication, navigation, weather forecasting, scientific research, and Earth observation. Additionally, navigation satellites transmit signals used by the Global Positioning System (GPS) to determine the location of objects on Earth. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>facilitating</u>과 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 위성 데이터는 글로벌 통신을 촉진하는(facilitating) 데 결정적 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ promoting: 촉진하다 — facilitating과 동의어
❌ ① preventing: 방지하다 — 반의어
❌ ② replacing: 대체하다 — 촉진과 다른 의미
❌ ④ monitoring: 모니터링하다 — 관찰이지 촉진이 아님
det.tip: facilitate = promote = help to advance (촉진하다, 용이하게 하다)

questions.passage: In conclusion, while satellite technology has <u>revolutionized</u> the world, it still has limitations and challenges.  Addressing these issues is crucial for building a promising future for space exploration.  The space industry also needs to share responsibility and collaborate to properly use satellite technology.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>revolutionized</u>와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: 위성 기술이 세계를 혁신시켰다(revolutionized).
det.analysis:
✅ ① transformed: 변혁시키다 — revolutionized와 동의어
❌ ② damaged: 손상시키다 — 반의어
❌ ③ maintained: 유지하다 — 변화와 반대
❌ ④ limited: 제한하다 — 혁신과 반대
det.tip: revolutionize = transform = bring about radical change (혁신하다, 변혁시키다)

questions.passage:
Challenges in Satellite Technology

The <u>increasing</u> number of satellites launched into orbit has caused problems, one of which is space debris.  Nearly half of the satellites in orbit are no longer in use.  However, they continue to orbit the Earth at high speeds and sometimes collide with other satellites.  These impacts have created up to 1 million pieces of space debris, which can damage satellites already in orbit and pose a threat to future space missions. 

Another problem is the light pollution from satellites.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>increasing</u>과 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 궤도로 발사되는 위성의 증가하는(increasing) 수가 문제를 일으키고 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ diminishing: 줄어드는 — increasing의 반의어
❌ ① rising: 오르는 — increasing의 동의어
❌ ② expanding: 확장하는 — increasing의 유의어
❌ ③ steady: 꾸준한 — 증감과 직접 반대 아님
det.tip: increasing(증가하는) ↔ diminishing(줄어드는). 오답 ①②는 동의어 함정

questions.passage: In conclusion, while satellite technology has revolutionized the world, it still has limitations and challenges.  Addressing these issues is crucial for building a promising future for space exploration.  The space industry also needs to share responsibility and <u>collaborate</u> to properly use satellite technology.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 <u>collaborate</u>와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 우주 산업은 위성 기술을 적절히 사용하기 위해 책임을 공유하고 협력해야(collaborate) 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ compete: 경쟁하다 — collaborate(협력하다)의 반의어
❌ ① cooperate: 협동하다 — collaborate의 동의어
❌ ② negotiate: 협상하다 — 협력과 유사한 맥락
❌ ④ communicate: 소통하다 — 협력의 전제이지 반의어 아님
det.tip: collaborate(협력하다) ↔ compete(경쟁하다). cooperate는 동의어 함정

questions.passage:
(A) <u>Addressing</u> these issues is crucial for building a promising future for space exploration. The space industry also needs to share responsibility.

(B) The scientist <u>addressed</u> the audience at the international conference, presenting new data on satellite debris collected over the past decade.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 address가 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) Addressing these issues = 이 문제들을 해결하는 것. (B) addressed the audience = 청중에게 연설했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 해결하다–연설하다: (A)는 문제(issues)를 대상으로 '해결/다루다', (B)는 청중(audience)을 대상으로 '연설하다'
❌ ① 연설하다–해결하다: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ 둘 다 해결하다: (B)에서 audience를 해결한다는 것은 부적합
❌ ④ 둘 다 연설하다: (A)에서 issues에게 연설한다는 것은 부적합
det.tip: address: ① (문제를) 다루다/해결하다 = deal with ② (청중에게) 연설하다 = speak to. 목적어가 issue/problem이면 '해결', person/audience이면 '연설'

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?

"the close observation of a person or group, especially by an authority, for the purpose of monitoring or gathering information"

det.korean: 특히 당국이 정보를 수집하거나 모니터링할 목적으로 사람이나 집단을 면밀히 관찰하는 것 → surveillance(감시)
det.analysis:
✅ ③ surveillance: 감시, 감찰 — authority, monitoring, gathering information에 부합
❌ ① navigation: 항해, 내비게이션 — 경로 안내
❌ ② communication: 통신 — 정보 교환
❌ ④ observation: 관찰 — 일반적 관찰로, authority/monitoring 목적 미포함
det.tip: surveillance = 감시, 감찰 (security 목적). observation은 일반적 관찰

questions.passage: This curiosity has led to the __________ (explore) of the universe, and as a result, space is no longer an unknown territory. Since the launch of the first artificial satellite, Sputnik 1, in 1957, the world has witnessed the blossoming of space exploration.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 호기심은 우주의 탐험(exploration)으로 이어졌다.
det.analysis: explore → exploration: 'the ______ of the universe'에서 관사 the 뒤 명사가 필요. 동사 explore의 명사형.
det.tip: explore(동사: 탐험하다) → exploration(명사: 탐험). the + 명사 + of 구조

questions.passage: In 2023, NEXTSAT-2 and seven other satellites were launched using a __________ (domestic) developed rocket, Nuri.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 국내에서(domestically) 개발된 로켓 누리호를 사용하여 발사되었다.
det.analysis: domestic → domestically: 과거분사 developed를 수식하는 부사 형태 필요. '국내에서 개발된'이라는 의미.
det.tip: domestic(형용사: 국내의) → domestically(부사: 국내에서). 분사(developed) 앞에 부사가 와야 한다.

questions.passage: In conclusion, while satellite technology has revolutionized the world, it still has limitations and challenges.  Addressing these issues is crucial for building a promising future for space exploration.  The space industry also needs to share responsibility and collaborate to properly use satellite technology.  Only then can we ensure __________, benefiting all humans on Earth.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 그래야만 우리는 자원과 정보의 균등한 분배(an equal distribution of resources and information)를 보장할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① an equal distribution of resources and information: 원문 그대로. 결론부에서 협력과 책임 공유의 목적
❌ ② fastest development: 빠른 발전이 아닌 균등 분배가 목적
❌ ③ complete elimination: 완전 제거는 비현실적 주장
❌ ④ dominance of one country: 한 나라의 지배는 본문 취지와 반대
det.tip: equal distribution = 균등한 분배. 본문의 uneven distribution 문제에 대한 해결책

ch: an equal distribution of resources and information
the fastest development of satellite technology
the complete elimination of space debris
the dominance of one country in space exploration

questions.passage:
It is predicted that by 2030, the night sky will be up to 12 percent brighter than its natural darkness.  This means that in the near future we may not be able to see the stars anymore. 

In addition, the development of satellite technology is closely tied to __________.  Some countries lack satellites or the capability to analyze satellite data, while others have launched hundreds of them and created a vast pool of information.  Approximately 37 percent of the global population remains unconnected to the internet, unable to fully benefit from satellite-based services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 위성 기술의 발전은 정보에 대한 불평등한 접근(unequal access to information)과 밀접하게 관련되어 있다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② unequal access to information: 원문 그대로. 일부 국가는 위성이 없고 다른 국가는 수백 개를 보유한다는 맥락
❌ ① rapid advancement: 빠른 발전은 문제가 아닌 성과
❌ ③ growing number of missions: 임무 증가 자체가 아닌 정보 불균등이 핵심
❌ ④ improved communication: 개선된 통신은 긍정적 내용으로 문제점과 불일치
det.tip: unequal access = 불평등한 접근. closely tied to = ~과 밀접하게 관련된

ch: the rapid advancement of satellite technology
the growing number of space missions
